+\emph{Distance estimate.}
+Thus $|hR_r-skb|\ge1$ in both chambers.  Equation

 \[

+\operatorname{dist}(beQ_{r-1},Q_r\mathbb Z)

+\begin{lemma}[Quadratic bounded sliding congruences]
+\label{lem:quadratic-sliding-congruences}
+Take either parameter chamber in
+Lemma~\ref{lem:quadratic-pisot-chambers}, let $d=\lfloor\beta\rfloor$, and
+let $(Q_j)$ be \eqref{eq:qminus} or \eqref{eq:qplus}.  If $m\ge3$ and
+$e_0,\ldots,e_{2m-2}\in[-d,d]\cap\mathbb Z$ satisfy
+\begin{equation}
+\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}Q_j e_{t+j}\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}
+\qquad(0\le t<m),
+\label{eq:sliding-kernel}
+\end{equation}
+then $e_0=\cdots=e_{2m-2}=0$.
+\end{lemma}
 
-\paragraph{Closure of the distance estimate.}
-For the nearest integer $k$ chosen above, \eqref{eq:nearest-error} is the
-exact identity
+\begin{proof}
+Write $s=1$ in the negative chamber and $s=-1$ in the positive chamber, so
+$Q_{j+2}=aQ_{j+1}+sbQ_j$, and put $\delta=Q_1-a$.  Subtracting $a$ times
+the congruence at $t+1$ and $sb$ times that at $t+2$ from the congruence at
+$t$ gives
+\begin{equation}
+e_t+\delta e_{t+1}-sbQ_{m-1}e_{t+m+1}\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}.
+\label{eq:quadratic-elimination}
+\end{equation}

+For $m\ge4$, the small part has modulus at most $d(1+\delta)$, whereas
 \[

+Q_{m-2}\ge Q_2=
+\begin{cases}

+a^2-b>a-1=d(1+\delta),&s=-1.
+\end{cases}

-Since $Q_{r-2}>0$, the chamberwise estimate gives $|E|\ge Q_{r-2}$.
-Finally, $kQ_r\in Q_r\mathbb Z$ and $k$ was chosen nearest to
-$beQ_{r-1}/Q_r$, so
+Lemma~\ref{lem:nearest-multiple-separation} therefore forces
+$e_{t+m+1}=0$ for $0\le t\le m-3$.  The last original congruence then gives
+$e_{m-1}+Q_1e_m=0$; since $Q_1>d$ and the left side has modulus below
+$Q_m$, both digits vanish.  Back substitution gives the remaining digits.
+
+At $m=3$, each window sum is $k_tQ_3$ with
+$k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}$.  Appendix~\ref{app:m3-triples} classifies the bounded
+solutions of one window equation in each chamber and compares their
+overlapping endpoint pairs.  The only three-window overlap is the zero one,
+so $e_0=\cdots=e_4=0$.
+\end{proof}

+\subsection{Sharp threshold and extremal bases}

+\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]
+\label{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}
+Let $\beta$ be an arbitrary quadratic Pisot number and use exactly the
+greedy language, Parry data, rank, cyclic modulus and fold of
+Definition~\ref{def:quadratic-parry-fold}.  Then
 \[

-=|beQ_{r-1}-kQ_r|=|E|\ge Q_{r-2}.
+m_*(\beta)=
+\begin{cases}
+3,&\beta\text{ is the root of }x^2-ax-a,\quad a\ge1,\\
+3,&\beta\text{ is the root of }x^2-ax+1,\quad a\ge3,\\
+2,&\text{otherwise}.
+\end{cases}

-This is \eqref{eq:quadratic-separation}.

-Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and

-Thus the kernel is trivial also at $m=3$.  The finite computation described in

-\subsection{Sharp threshold and extremal bases}

-\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]
-\label{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}
-Let $\beta$ be an arbitrary quadratic Pisot number and use exactly the
-greedy language, Parry data, rank, cyclic modulus and fold of
-Definition~\ref{def:quadratic-parry-fold}.  Then
-\[

-\begin{equation}

-$(\lfloor\beta\rfloor+1)$-shift onto the SFT $Y_{\beta,m}$, with inverse of
-memory zero and anticipation $m-1$.
-

-Pisot family is three.  Its extremizers are exactly the negative-conjugate
-diagonal $P^-_{a,a}$ and the positive-conjugate norm-one family
-$P^+_{a,1}$.  The golden mean is the least extremizer, but it is not the
-unique extremizer after passage from metallic units to all quadratic Pisot
-bases.
-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}

-length-$m$ finite-block map injective.  Consecutive decoded blocks cover a
-longer raw block, proving injectivity for every $n\ge m$ and the count

+from two output symbols.

+\begin{proof}

-\[

+\section{Finite quadratic arithmetic}
+\label{app:quadratic-arithmetic}
+
+\subsection{The positive-recurrence integer exclusion}
+\label{app:positive-integer-exclusion}
+
+We prove Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.  Put
+\[
+S=a^2+a+b,qquad T=a^3+a^2+2ab+b=aS+b(a+1).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+U_+-a=\frac{b(a+1)}S,qquad L_+-a=\frac{bS}T.
+\]
+For $h=be-ak>0$, divide
+\[
+be=aq+r,qquad qb=ap+t,qquad 0\le r,t<a.
+\]
+Here $0\le q\le b$, and $q\le b-1$ when $r>0$.  If $k\le q-1$, then
+$h\ge a+r$ and
+\[
+hL_+-kb>(a+r)a-(b-1)b\ge a^2-b(b-1)\ge1.
+\]
+The inequality $k\ge q+1$ would give $h<0$.  Hence $k=q$ and $h=r$.
+Writing $j=kb-ah=a(p-r)+t$, the cases $p<r$ and $p>r$ give respectively
+\[
+rL_+-qb=a(r-p)-t+r(L_+-a)>a-t\ge1
+\]
+and
+\[
+qb-rU_+=a(p-r)+t-r(U_+-a)
+>a-\frac{rb}{a}\ge a-b+\frac ba\ge1.
+\]
+
+It remains to treat $p=r$.  Put $w=rb-at$.  The divisions give
+\begin{equation}
+b^2e=r(a^2+b)+at,qquad w=r(a^2+2b)-b^2e.
+\label{eq:app-terminal-divisions}
+\end{equation}
+The integer $w$ cannot vanish.  Indeed, if $a=gA$, $b=gB$ with
+$(A,B)=1$, then $at=rb$ gives $r=AR$, $t=BR$ with $0<R<g$; reduction of
+the first two divisions modulo $g$ and Bezout's identity force $g\mid R$.
+
+Make one further division
+\[
+rb=au+v,qquad 0\le v<a.
+\]
+Then $w=a(u-t)+v$.  Substitution in the three reversed divisions shows
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c}
+\text{sign of }w&\text{quotient relation}&\text{remainder inequality}\\ \hline
+w>0&u-t\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w>0&u-t=1&av\ge b(t+1)\\
+w<0&t-u\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w<0&t-u=1&b(t-1)\ge v(a+1).
+\end{array}
+\]
+For the two boundary rows, substitute $u=t+1$ or $u=t-1$ successively into
+\[
+r=\frac{au+v}{b},\qquad q=\frac{ar+t}{b},\qquad
+e=\frac{aq+r}{b}.
+\]
+After multiplication by $b,b^2,b^3$, failure of the stated remainder
+inequality forces $r\ge a$, $q>b$, or a nonintegral final quotient.  If an
+equality occurs before the last division, write again $a=gA$, $b=gB$; the
+remaining quotient lies strictly between $0$ and $g$, while the three
+divisibilities force it to be divisible by $g$.  This establishes the four
+alternatives without assuming $(a,b)=1$.
+
+Define
+\begin{align*}
+\Delta_L&=rbS-(t+1)T=T\{r(L_+-a)-t-1\},\\
+\Delta_U&=tS-rb(a+1)-S=S\{t-r(U_+-a)-1\}.
+\end{align*}
+Using $T=aS+b(a+1)$ gives
+\[
+\Delta_L=wS-T-tb(a+1),qquad
+\Delta_U=tb+(-w)(a+1)-S.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_L\ge2aS-T-(a-1)b(a+1)=a^2(a-b+1)>0.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t=1$, the remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_L=vS-b(a+1)(t+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$r(L_+-a)-t\ge1$.
+
+If $w<0$ and $t-u\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_U\ge(a+1)^2-S=a+1-b\ge1.
+\]
+If $w<0$ and $t-u=1$, the last remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_U=b(t-1)-v(a+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$t-r(U_+-a)\ge1$.  Since $w\ne0$, one of these alternatives applies and
+proves Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.
+
+\subsection{The aperture-three triple classification}
+\label{app:m3-triples}
+
+For $m=3$, write each congruence in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} as
+\[
+e_t+Q_1e_{t+1}+Q_2e_{t+2}=k_tQ_3,qquad
+k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}.
+\]
+
+In the negative-conjugate chamber,
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a+1,a^2+a+b,a^3+a^2+2ab+b),qquad |e_j|\le a.
+\]
+For one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$, sign symmetry reduces to $k=0,1$.
+When $k=0$, the bound $2Q_2>a(1+Q_1)$ gives $|z|\le1$; $z=0$ gives
+$(x,y)=(0,0)$, and $z=1$ gives $(x,y)=(-b,-a)$.  When $k=1$, the bound
+at $z\le a-1$ forces $z=a$, after which
+$x+(a+1)y=b(a+1)$ gives $(x,y)=(0,b)$.  Hence the solution list is
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(b,a,-1;0),\ \pm(0,b,a;1)\}.
+\]
+Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(a,-1)$, and $\pm(b,a)$.  A final
+triple of type $\pm(0,b,a)$ has initial pair $\pm(0,b)$, which is not a
+terminal pair.  A final triple of type $\pm(b,a,-1)$ forces the preceding
+triple to be $\pm(0,b,a)$, whose initial pair again cannot be terminal.
+
+In the positive-conjugate chamber put $C=a-b$ and $d=a-1$.  Then
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a,a^2-b,a^3-2ab),qquad 2\le C\le d.
+\]
+For $x+ay+Q_2z=kQ_3$, the same bounds give
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(C,d,-1;0),
+\ \pm(-b,C,d;1),\ \pm(C,C-1,d;1)\}.
+\]
+Indeed, for $k=0$ one has $|z|\le1$, and $z=1$ forces
+$(x,y)=(-C,-d)$.  For $k=1$, the inequality at $z\le a-2$ forces $z=d$;
+reducing $x+ay=aC-b$ modulo $a$ leaves precisely
+$(x,y)=(-b,C)$ and $(C,C-1)$.  The terminal pairs are
+$(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and $\pm(C-1,d)$.  Neither
+$\pm(-b,C)$ nor $\pm(C,C-1)$ is terminal.  The remaining type
+$\pm(C,d,-1)$ forces a preceding $\pm(-b,C,d)$, whose initial pair is not
+terminal.
+
+Thus, in either chamber, a nonzero triple cannot persist through all three
+overlaps.  Reading the three equations backwards forces
+$e_2=e_3=e_4=0$, then $e_1=0$, and finally $e_0=0$.

 \begin{abstract}
-We determine exact overlap thresholds and local inverse structure for cyclic
-language-rank recodings of quadratic and simple-Parry beta-languages.  A

-$(a,b,d,c_0)=(4,2,3,1)$,

-\begin{remark}[What is and is not claimed]
-\label{rem:quadratic-open-interface}
-The theorem concerns the cyclic language-rank recoding of
-Definition~\ref{def:quadratic-parry-fold}.  Published finite-transducer
-normalization results for Pisot bases
-\cite{Frougny1992,FrougnySteiner2008,BertheFrougnyRigoSakarovitch2019}
-establish recognizability for numerical representations on other redundant
-digit sets and boundary conventions, but they do not identify those
-normalizations with this cyclic rank map.
-No threshold claim is made for signed digits, non-greedy expansions,
-non-cyclic truncation, degree greater than two, or general Pisot substitution
-codings.  These choices are genuine residual interfaces rather than
-consequences of Theorem~\ref{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}.
-\end{remark}

+\label{eq:quadratic-elimination}
+\end{equation}
+
+For $m\ge4$, the small part has modulus at most $d(1+\delta)$, whereas
 \[
-E=beQ_{r-1}-kQ_r=(hR_r-skb)Q_{r-2}.
+Q_{m-2}\ge Q_2=
+\begin{cases}
+a^2+a+b>2a=d(1+\delta),&s=1,\\
+a^2-b>a-1=d(1+\delta),&s=-1.
+\end{cases}
 \]
-Since $Q_{r-2}>0$, the chamberwise estimate gives $|E|\ge Q_{r-2}$.
-Finally, $kQ_r\in Q_r\mathbb Z$ and $k$ was chosen nearest to
-$beQ_{r-1}/Q_r$, so
+Lemma~\ref{lem:nearest-multiple-separation} therefore forces
+$e_{t+m+1}=0$ for $0\le t\le m-3$.  The last original congruence then gives
+$e_{m-1}+Q_1e_m=0$; since $Q_1>d$ and the left side has modulus below
+$Q_m$, both digits vanish.  Back substitution gives the remaining digits.
+
+At $m=3$, each window sum is $k_tQ_3$ with
+$k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}$.  Appendix~\ref{app:m3-triples} classifies the bounded
+solutions of one window equation in each chamber and compares their
+overlapping endpoint pairs.  The only three-window overlap is the zero one,
+so $e_0=\cdots=e_4=0$.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]
+\label{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}
+Let $\beta$ be an arbitrary quadratic Pisot number and use exactly the
+greedy language, Parry data, rank, cyclic modulus and fold of

 \[

-=|beQ_{r-1}-kQ_r|=|E|\ge Q_{r-2}.
+m_*(\beta)=
+\begin{cases}
+3,&\beta\text{ is the root of }x^2-ax-a,\quad a\ge1,\\
+3,&\beta\text{ is the root of }x^2-ax+1,\quad a\ge3,\\
+2,&\text{otherwise}.
+\end{cases}

-This is \eqref{eq:quadratic-separation}.
-\end{proof}

-The following sliding lemma is the arithmetic core of the block decoder.

-\begin{lemma}[Quadratic bounded sliding congruences]
-\label{lem:quadratic-sliding-congruences}
-Take either parameter chamber in
-Lemma~\ref{lem:quadratic-pisot-chambers}, let $d=\lfloor\beta\rfloor$, and
-let $(Q_j)$ be \eqref{eq:qminus} or \eqref{eq:qplus}.  If $m\ge3$ and
-$e_0,\ldots,e_{2m-2}\in[-d,d]\cap\mathbb Z$ satisfy
-\begin{equation}
-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}Q_j e_{t+j}\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}
-\qquad(0\le t<m),\label{eq:sliding-kernel}
-\end{equation}
-then $e_0=\cdots=e_{2m-2}=0$.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Write $s=1$ in the negative chamber and $s=-1$ in the positive chamber, so
-$Q_{j+2}=aQ_{j+1}+sbQ_j$, and put
-$\delta=Q_1-a$; hence $(d,\delta)=(a,1)$ for $s=1$ and
-$(d,\delta)=(a-1,0)$ for $s=-1$.  Subtracting $a$ times the congruence at
-$t+1$ and $sb$ times that at $t+2$ from the congruence at $t$ cancels every
-interior coefficient and gives
-\begin{equation}
-e_t+\delta e_{t+1}-sbQ_{m-1}e_{t+m+1}\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}.
-\label{eq:quadratic-elimination}
-\end{equation}
-
-Suppose first that $m\ge4$.  The small part of
-\eqref{eq:quadratic-elimination} has modulus at most
-$d(1+\delta)$.  On the other hand,
-\[
-Q_{m-2}\ge Q_2=
-\begin{cases}
-a^2+a+b>2a=d(1+\delta),&s=1,\\
-a^2-b>a-1=d(1+\delta),&s=-1.
-\end{cases}
-\]
-Lemma~\ref{lem:nearest-multiple-separation} therefore gives a strictly larger
-distance whenever $e_{t+m+1}\ne0$.  Hence
-$e_{t+m+1}=0$ for $0\le t\le m-3$.  Thus
-$e_{m+1}=\cdots=e_{2m-2}=0$.  The final original congruence reduces to
-\[
-e_{m-1}+Q_1e_m\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}.
-\]
-Its left side has modulus at most $d(1+Q_1)<Q_m$ and $Q_1>d$, so both
-digits vanish.  Back substitution in the preceding congruences then gives
-$e_{m-2},\ldots,e_0=0$ successively.
-
-It remains to check $m=3$, where endpoint equality in the separation bound
-can occur.  Here each integer sum in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} has modulus
-less than $2Q_3$, so it is $k_tQ_3$ with $k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}$.  Substituting
-the three values of $t$ gives
-\begin{equation}

-\label{eq:quadratic-m3-equalities}
-\end{equation}
-We now eliminate the two conjugate signs separately.
-
-Suppose first that $s=1$.  Thus $d=a$ and
-\[

-Consider one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$ occurring in

-Consequently every bounded solution of one equation is
-\[

-\[

-\[

-\[

-Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and

+\section{Finite quadratic arithmetic}
+\label{app:quadratic-arithmetic}
+
+\subsection{The positive-recurrence integer exclusion}
+\label{app:positive-integer-exclusion}
+
+We prove Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.  Put
+\[
+S=a^2+a+b,qquad T=a^3+a^2+2ab+b=aS+b(a+1).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+U_+-a=\frac{b(a+1)}S,qquad L_+-a=\frac{bS}T.
+\]
+For $h=be-ak>0$, divide
+\[
+be=aq+r,qquad qb=ap+t,qquad 0\le r,t<a.
+\]
+Here $0\le q\le b$, and $q\le b-1$ when $r>0$.  If $k\le q-1$, then
+$h\ge a+r$ and
+\[
+hL_+-kb>(a+r)a-(b-1)b\ge a^2-b(b-1)\ge1.
+\]
+The inequality $k\ge q+1$ would give $h<0$.  Hence $k=q$ and $h=r$.
+Writing $j=kb-ah=a(p-r)+t$, the cases $p<r$ and $p>r$ give respectively
+\[
+rL_+-qb=a(r-p)-t+r(L_+-a)>a-t\ge1
+\]
+and
+\[
+qb-rU_+=a(p-r)+t-r(U_+-a)
+>a-\frac{rb}{a}\ge a-b+\frac ba\ge1.
+\]
+
+It remains to treat $p=r$.  Put $w=rb-at$.  The divisions give
+\begin{equation}
+b^2e=r(a^2+b)+at,qquad w=r(a^2+2b)-b^2e.
+\label{eq:app-terminal-divisions}
+\end{equation}
+The integer $w$ cannot vanish.  Indeed, if $a=gA$, $b=gB$ with
+$(A,B)=1$, then $at=rb$ gives $r=AR$, $t=BR$ with $0<R<g$; reduction of
+the first two divisions modulo $g$ and Bezout's identity force $g\mid R$.
+
+Make one further division
+\[
+rb=au+v,qquad 0\le v<a.
+\]
+Then $w=a(u-t)+v$.  Substitution in the three reversed divisions shows
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c}
+\text{sign of }w&\text{quotient relation}&\text{remainder inequality}\\ \hline
+w>0&u-t\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w>0&u-t=1&av\ge b(t+1)\\
+w<0&t-u\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w<0&t-u=1&b(t-1)\ge v(a+1).
+\end{array}
+\]
+For the two boundary rows, substitute $u=t+1$ or $u=t-1$ successively into
+\[
+r=\frac{au+v}{b},\qquad q=\frac{ar+t}{b},\qquad
+e=\frac{aq+r}{b}.
+\]
+After multiplication by $b,b^2,b^3$, failure of the stated remainder
+inequality forces $r\ge a$, $q>b$, or a nonintegral final quotient.  If an
+equality occurs before the last division, write again $a=gA$, $b=gB$; the
+remaining quotient lies strictly between $0$ and $g$, while the three
+divisibilities force it to be divisible by $g$.  This establishes the four
+alternatives without assuming $(a,b)=1$.
+
+Define
+\begin{align*}
+\Delta_L&=rbS-(t+1)T=T\{r(L_+-a)-t-1\},\\
+\Delta_U&=tS-rb(a+1)-S=S\{t-r(U_+-a)-1\}.
+\end{align*}
+Using $T=aS+b(a+1)$ gives
+\[
+\Delta_L=wS-T-tb(a+1),qquad
+\Delta_U=tb+(-w)(a+1)-S.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_L\ge2aS-T-(a-1)b(a+1)=a^2(a-b+1)>0.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t=1$, the remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_L=vS-b(a+1)(t+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$r(L_+-a)-t\ge1$.
+
+If $w<0$ and $t-u\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_U\ge(a+1)^2-S=a+1-b\ge1.
+\]
+If $w<0$ and $t-u=1$, the last remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_U=b(t-1)-v(a+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$t-r(U_+-a)\ge1$.  Since $w\ne0$, one of these alternatives applies and
+proves Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.
+
+\subsection{The aperture-three triple classification}
+\label{app:m3-triples}
+
+For $m=3$, write each congruence in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} as
+\[
+e_t+Q_1e_{t+1}+Q_2e_{t+2}=k_tQ_3,qquad
+k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}.
+\]
+
+In the negative-conjugate chamber,
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a+1,a^2+a+b,a^3+a^2+2ab+b),qquad |e_j|\le a.
+\]
+For one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$, sign symmetry reduces to $k=0,1$.
+When $k=0$, the bound $2Q_2>a(1+Q_1)$ gives $|z|\le1$; $z=0$ gives
+$(x,y)=(0,0)$, and $z=1$ gives $(x,y)=(-b,-a)$.  When $k=1$, the bound
+at $z\le a-1$ forces $z=a$, after which
+$x+(a+1)y=b(a+1)$ gives $(x,y)=(0,b)$.  Hence the solution list is
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(b,a,-1;0),\ \pm(0,b,a;1)\}.
+\]
+Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(a,-1)$, and $\pm(b,a)$.  A final
+triple of type $\pm(0,b,a)$ has initial pair $\pm(0,b)$, which is not a
+terminal pair.  A final triple of type $\pm(b,a,-1)$ forces the preceding
+triple to be $\pm(0,b,a)$, whose initial pair again cannot be terminal.
+
+In the positive-conjugate chamber put $C=a-b$ and $d=a-1$.  Then
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a,a^2-b,a^3-2ab),qquad 2\le C\le d.
+\]
+For $x+ay+Q_2z=kQ_3$, the same bounds give
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(C,d,-1;0),
+\ \pm(-b,C,d;1),\ \pm(C,C-1,d;1)\}.
+\]
+Indeed, for $k=0$ one has $|z|\le1$, and $z=1$ forces
+$(x,y)=(-C,-d)$.  For $k=1$, the inequality at $z\le a-2$ forces $z=d$;
+reducing $x+ay=aC-b$ modulo $a$ leaves precisely
+$(x,y)=(-b,C)$ and $(C,C-1)$.  The terminal pairs are
+$(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and $\pm(C-1,d)$.  Neither
+$\pm(-b,C)$ nor $\pm(C,C-1)$ is terminal.  The remaining type
+$\pm(C,d,-1)$ forces a preceding $\pm(-b,C,d)$, whose initial pair is not
+terminal.
+
+Thus, in either chamber, a nonzero triple cannot persist through all three
+overlaps.  Reading the three equations backwards forces
+$e_2=e_3=e_4=0$, then $e_1=0$, and finally $e_0=0$.

 \begin{abstract}
-We determine exact overlap thresholds and local inverse structure for cyclic
-language-rank recodings of quadratic and simple-Parry beta-languages.  A
-legal length-$m$ word is identified with its colexicographic positional rank;
-the same rank is evaluated on the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number
-of legal words, returned to the legal language, and overlapped along the
-shift.  This is cyclic reduction of integer language ranks, not numerical
-$\beta$-normalization.
-

-two-window branch locus.  For every quadratic Pisot base, the least

-Markov order in the stabilized alphabet.  The metallic family becomes a
-transparent specialization of this classification.
+We study sliding recodings obtained by reducing colexicographic language

+\end{lemma}

+\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]
+\label{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}

+\section{Finite quadratic arithmetic}
+\label{app:quadratic-arithmetic}
+
+\subsection{The positive-recurrence integer exclusion}
+\label{app:positive-integer-exclusion}
+
+We prove Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.  Put
+\[
+S=a^2+a+b,qquad T=a^3+a^2+2ab+b=aS+b(a+1).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+U_+-a=\frac{b(a+1)}S,qquad L_+-a=\frac{bS}T.
+\]
+For $h=be-ak>0$, divide
+\[
+be=aq+r,qquad qb=ap+t,qquad 0\le r,t<a.
+\]
+Here $0\le q\le b$, and $q\le b-1$ when $r>0$.  If $k\le q-1$, then
+$h\ge a+r$ and
+\[
+hL_+-kb>(a+r)a-(b-1)b\ge a^2-b(b-1)\ge1.
+\]
+The inequality $k\ge q+1$ would give $h<0$.  Hence $k=q$ and $h=r$.
+Writing $j=kb-ah=a(p-r)+t$, the cases $p<r$ and $p>r$ give respectively
+\[
+rL_+-qb=a(r-p)-t+r(L_+-a)>a-t\ge1
+\]
+and
+\[
+qb-rU_+=a(p-r)+t-r(U_+-a)
+>a-\frac{rb}{a}\ge a-b+\frac ba\ge1.
+\]
+
+It remains to treat $p=r$.  Put $w=rb-at$.  The divisions give
+\begin{equation}
+b^2e=r(a^2+b)+at,qquad w=r(a^2+2b)-b^2e.
+\label{eq:app-terminal-divisions}
+\end{equation}
+The integer $w$ cannot vanish.  Indeed, if $a=gA$, $b=gB$ with
+$(A,B)=1$, then $at=rb$ gives $r=AR$, $t=BR$ with $0<R<g$; reduction of
+the first two divisions modulo $g$ and Bezout's identity force $g\mid R$.
+
+Make one further division
+\[
+rb=au+v,qquad 0\le v<a.
+\]
+Then $w=a(u-t)+v$.  Substitution in the three reversed divisions shows
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c}
+\text{sign of }w&\text{quotient relation}&\text{remainder inequality}\\ \hline
+w>0&u-t\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w>0&u-t=1&av\ge b(t+1)\\
+w<0&t-u\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w<0&t-u=1&b(t-1)\ge v(a+1).
+\end{array}
+\]
+For the two boundary rows, substitute $u=t+1$ or $u=t-1$ successively into
+\[
+r=\frac{au+v}{b},\qquad q=\frac{ar+t}{b},\qquad
+e=\frac{aq+r}{b}.
+\]
+After multiplication by $b,b^2,b^3$, failure of the stated remainder
+inequality forces $r\ge a$, $q>b$, or a nonintegral final quotient.  If an
+equality occurs before the last division, write again $a=gA$, $b=gB$; the
+remaining quotient lies strictly between $0$ and $g$, while the three
+divisibilities force it to be divisible by $g$.  This establishes the four
+alternatives without assuming $(a,b)=1$.
+
+Define
+\begin{align*}
+\Delta_L&=rbS-(t+1)T=T\{r(L_+-a)-t-1\},\\
+\Delta_U&=tS-rb(a+1)-S=S\{t-r(U_+-a)-1\}.
+\end{align*}
+Using $T=aS+b(a+1)$ gives
+\[
+\Delta_L=wS-T-tb(a+1),qquad
+\Delta_U=tb+(-w)(a+1)-S.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_L\ge2aS-T-(a-1)b(a+1)=a^2(a-b+1)>0.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t=1$, the remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_L=vS-b(a+1)(t+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$r(L_+-a)-t\ge1$.
+
+If $w<0$ and $t-u\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_U\ge(a+1)^2-S=a+1-b\ge1.
+\]
+If $w<0$ and $t-u=1$, the last remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_U=b(t-1)-v(a+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$t-r(U_+-a)\ge1$.  Since $w\ne0$, one of these alternatives applies and
+proves Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.

+\subsection{The aperture-three triple classification}
+\label{app:m3-triples}
+
+For $m=3$, write each congruence in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} as
+\[
+e_t+Q_1e_{t+1}+Q_2e_{t+2}=k_tQ_3,qquad
+k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}.
+\]
+
+In the negative-conjugate chamber,
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a+1,a^2+a+b,a^3+a^2+2ab+b),qquad |e_j|\le a.
+\]
+For one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$, sign symmetry reduces to $k=0,1$.
+When $k=0$, the bound $2Q_2>a(1+Q_1)$ gives $|z|\le1$; $z=0$ gives
+$(x,y)=(0,0)$, and $z=1$ gives $(x,y)=(-b,-a)$.  When $k=1$, the bound
+at $z\le a-1$ forces $z=a$, after which
+$x+(a+1)y=b(a+1)$ gives $(x,y)=(0,b)$.  Hence the solution list is
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(b,a,-1;0),\ \pm(0,b,a;1)\}.
+\]
+Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(a,-1)$, and $\pm(b,a)$.  A final
+triple of type $\pm(0,b,a)$ has initial pair $\pm(0,b)$, which is not a
+terminal pair.  A final triple of type $\pm(b,a,-1)$ forces the preceding
+triple to be $\pm(0,b,a)$, whose initial pair again cannot be terminal.
+
+In the positive-conjugate chamber put $C=a-b$ and $d=a-1$.  Then
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a,a^2-b,a^3-2ab),qquad 2\le C\le d.
+\]
+For $x+ay+Q_2z=kQ_3$, the same bounds give
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(C,d,-1;0),
+\ \pm(-b,C,d;1),\ \pm(C,C-1,d;1)\}.
+\]
+Indeed, for $k=0$ one has $|z|\le1$, and $z=1$ forces
+$(x,y)=(-C,-d)$.  For $k=1$, the inequality at $z\le a-2$ forces $z=d$;
+reducing $x+ay=aC-b$ modulo $a$ leaves precisely
+$(x,y)=(-b,C)$ and $(C,C-1)$.  The terminal pairs are
+$(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and $\pm(C-1,d)$.  Neither
+$\pm(-b,C)$ nor $\pm(C,C-1)$ is terminal.  The remaining type
+$\pm(C,d,-1)$ forces a preceding $\pm(-b,C,d)$, whose initial pair is not
+terminal.
+
+Thus, in either chamber, a nonzero triple cannot persist through all three
+overlaps.  Reading the three equations backwards forces
+$e_2=e_3=e_4=0$, then $e_1=0$, and finally $e_0=0$.

\begin{theorem}[Bassino family: unbounded future-only inverse length]
\label{thm:cubic-unbounded-causal-depth}
For Bassino's family, let $n\ge4$, let $\beta_n\in(n,n+1)$ be the root of
\eqref{eq:cubic-unbounded-polynomial} and put $m_n=n-1$.  Then $\beta_n$
is a nonintegral cubic simple-Parry Pisot number, $\Phi_{\beta_n,m_n}$ is
injective, and
\begin{equation}
\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta_n,m_n)=n-1.
\label{eq:cubic-unbounded-causal-length}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\[
\sup\left\{\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m):
\substack{\beta\text{ nonintegral cubic simple-Parry Pisot},\\
m\ge2,\ \Phi_{\beta,m}\text{ injective}}\right\}=\infty.
\]
\end{theorem}

+\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]

 \[

-\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]
-\label{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}
-Let $\beta$ be an arbitrary quadratic Pisot number and use exactly the
-greedy language, Parry data, rank, cyclic modulus and fold of
-Definition~\ref{def:quadratic-parry-fold}.  Then
-\[

-\end{cases}

-$(\lfloor\beta\rfloor+1)$-shift onto the SFT $Y_{\beta,m}$, with inverse of
-memory zero and anticipation $m-1$.

-Pisot family is three.  Its extremizers are exactly the negative-conjugate
-diagonal $P^-_{a,a}$ and the positive-conjugate norm-one family
-$P^+_{a,1}$.  The golden mean is the least extremizer, but it is not the
-unique extremizer after passage from metallic units to all quadratic Pisot
-bases.
-\end{theorem}

-length-$m$ finite-block map injective.  Consecutive decoded blocks cover a
-longer raw block, proving injectivity for every $n\ge m$ and the count

+\begin{proof}

+\section{Finite quadratic arithmetic}
+\label{app:quadratic-arithmetic}
+
+\subsection{The positive-recurrence integer exclusion}
+\label{app:positive-integer-exclusion}
+
+We prove Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.  Put
+\[
+S=a^2+a+b,qquad T=a^3+a^2+2ab+b=aS+b(a+1).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+U_+-a=\frac{b(a+1)}S,qquad L_+-a=\frac{bS}T.
+\]
+For $h=be-ak>0$, divide
+\[
+be=aq+r,qquad qb=ap+t,qquad 0\le r,t<a.
+\]
+Here $0\le q\le b$, and $q\le b-1$ when $r>0$.  If $k\le q-1$, then
+$h\ge a+r$ and
+\[
+hL_+-kb>(a+r)a-(b-1)b\ge a^2-b(b-1)\ge1.
+\]
+The inequality $k\ge q+1$ would give $h<0$.  Hence $k=q$ and $h=r$.
+Writing $j=kb-ah=a(p-r)+t$, the cases $p<r$ and $p>r$ give respectively
+\[
+rL_+-qb=a(r-p)-t+r(L_+-a)>a-t\ge1
+\]
+and
+\[
+qb-rU_+=a(p-r)+t-r(U_+-a)
+>a-\frac{rb}{a}\ge a-b+\frac ba\ge1.
+\]
+
+It remains to treat $p=r$.  Put $w=rb-at$.  The divisions give
+\begin{equation}
+b^2e=r(a^2+b)+at,qquad w=r(a^2+2b)-b^2e.
+\label{eq:app-terminal-divisions}
+\end{equation}
+The integer $w$ cannot vanish.  Indeed, if $a=gA$, $b=gB$ with
+$(A,B)=1$, then $at=rb$ gives $r=AR$, $t=BR$ with $0<R<g$; reduction of
+the first two divisions modulo $g$ and Bezout's identity force $g\mid R$.
+
+Make one further division
+\[
+rb=au+v,qquad 0\le v<a.
+\]
+Then $w=a(u-t)+v$.  Substitution in the three reversed divisions shows
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c}
+\text{sign of }w&\text{quotient relation}&\text{remainder inequality}\\ \hline
+w>0&u-t\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w>0&u-t=1&av\ge b(t+1)\\
+w<0&t-u\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w<0&t-u=1&b(t-1)\ge v(a+1).
+\end{array}
+\]
+For the two boundary rows, substitute $u=t+1$ or $u=t-1$ successively into
+\[
+r=\frac{au+v}{b},\qquad q=\frac{ar+t}{b},\qquad
+e=\frac{aq+r}{b}.
+\]
+After multiplication by $b,b^2,b^3$, failure of the stated remainder
+inequality forces $r\ge a$, $q>b$, or a nonintegral final quotient.  If an
+equality occurs before the last division, write again $a=gA$, $b=gB$; the
+remaining quotient lies strictly between $0$ and $g$, while the three
+divisibilities force it to be divisible by $g$.  This establishes the four
+alternatives without assuming $(a,b)=1$.
+
+Define
+\begin{align*}
+\Delta_L&=rbS-(t+1)T=T\{r(L_+-a)-t-1\},\\
+\Delta_U&=tS-rb(a+1)-S=S\{t-r(U_+-a)-1\}.
+\end{align*}
+Using $T=aS+b(a+1)$ gives
+\[
+\Delta_L=wS-T-tb(a+1),qquad
+\Delta_U=tb+(-w)(a+1)-S.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_L\ge2aS-T-(a-1)b(a+1)=a^2(a-b+1)>0.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t=1$, the remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_L=vS-b(a+1)(t+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$r(L_+-a)-t\ge1$.
+
+If $w<0$ and $t-u\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_U\ge(a+1)^2-S=a+1-b\ge1.
+\]
+If $w<0$ and $t-u=1$, the last remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_U=b(t-1)-v(a+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$t-r(U_+-a)\ge1$.  Since $w\ne0$, one of these alternatives applies and
+proves Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.

+\subsection{The aperture-three triple classification}
+\label{app:m3-triples}
+
+For $m=3$, write each congruence in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} as
+\[
+e_t+Q_1e_{t+1}+Q_2e_{t+2}=k_tQ_3,qquad
+k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}.
+\]
+
+In the negative-conjugate chamber,
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a+1,a^2+a+b,a^3+a^2+2ab+b),qquad |e_j|\le a.
+\]
+For one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$, sign symmetry reduces to $k=0,1$.
+When $k=0$, the bound $2Q_2>a(1+Q_1)$ gives $|z|\le1$; $z=0$ gives
+$(x,y)=(0,0)$, and $z=1$ gives $(x,y)=(-b,-a)$.  When $k=1$, the bound
+at $z\le a-1$ forces $z=a$, after which
+$x+(a+1)y=b(a+1)$ gives $(x,y)=(0,b)$.  Hence the solution list is
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(b,a,-1;0),\ \pm(0,b,a;1)\}.
+\]
+Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(a,-1)$, and $\pm(b,a)$.  A final
+triple of type $\pm(0,b,a)$ has initial pair $\pm(0,b)$, which is not a
+terminal pair.  A final triple of type $\pm(b,a,-1)$ forces the preceding
+triple to be $\pm(0,b,a)$, whose initial pair again cannot be terminal.
+
+In the positive-conjugate chamber put $C=a-b$ and $d=a-1$.  Then
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a,a^2-b,a^3-2ab),qquad 2\le C\le d.
+\]
+For $x+ay+Q_2z=kQ_3$, the same bounds give
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(C,d,-1;0),
+\ \pm(-b,C,d;1),\ \pm(C,C-1,d;1)\}.
+\]
+Indeed, for $k=0$ one has $|z|\le1$, and $z=1$ forces
+$(x,y)=(-C,-d)$.  For $k=1$, the inequality at $z\le a-2$ forces $z=d$;
+reducing $x+ay=aC-b$ modulo $a$ leaves precisely
+$(x,y)=(-b,C)$ and $(C,C-1)$.  The terminal pairs are
+$(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and $\pm(C-1,d)$.  Neither
+$\pm(-b,C)$ nor $\pm(C,C-1)$ is terminal.  The remaining type
+$\pm(C,d,-1)$ forces a preceding $\pm(-b,C,d)$, whose initial pair is not
+terminal.
+
+Thus, in either chamber, a nonzero triple cannot persist through all three
+overlaps.  Reading the three equations backwards forces
+$e_2=e_3=e_4=0$, then $e_1=0$, and finally $e_0=0$.

 \begin{abstract}
-We determine exact overlap thresholds and local inverse structure for cyclic
-language-rank recodings of quadratic and simple-Parry beta-languages.  A
-legal length-$m$ word is identified with its colexicographic positional rank;
-the same rank is evaluated on the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number
-of legal words, returned to the legal language, and overlapped along the
-shift.  This is cyclic reduction of integer language ranks, not numerical
-$\beta$-normalization.
-
-The Fibonacci model has sharp nontrivial threshold three.  We give its
-explicit three-window decoder, low-window counterexamples, and complete
-two-window branch locus.  For every quadratic Pisot base, the least
-nontrivial aperture is three exactly for the roots of
-$x^2-ax-a$ and $x^2-ax+1$, and is two otherwise.  We also determine chamber
-duality, future-only inverse bounds, the critical two-fixed-point normal
-form, exact finite-block onset, the canonical right Fischer cover, and exact
-Markov order in the stabilized alphabet.  The metallic family becomes a
-transparent specialization of this classification.
+We study sliding recodings obtained by reducing colexicographic language
+ranks modulo the number of legal words and overlapping the resulting finite
+windows.  For every quadratic Pisot $\beta$-language, the least nontrivial
+injective aperture is three precisely for the roots of $x^2-ax-a$ and
+$x^2-ax+1$, and is two otherwise.  The future-only inverse length is three in
+the positive-conjugate chamber and two in the negative chamber at aperture
+three; for negative conjugate and aperture $m\ge4$ we prove the bounds
+$2\le\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)\le m$.
 
 For every nonintegral simple-Parry base, a coordinatewise-difference quotient
-of the classical pair graph preserves every collision and gives an exact
-longest-path formula for future-only inverse depth.  We derive the complete
-aperture-two trichotomy without a Pisot hypothesis.  Applied to Bassino's
-cubic simple-Parry Pisot family, the quotient gives injective apertures
-$m_n=n-1$ with exact future-only inverse length $n-1$, hence unbounded depth
-across the family.
+of the classical pair graph preserves all collisions.  Its longest directed
+paths give the future-only inverse length, while reachable cycles decide
+noninjectivity; the resulting aperture-two trichotomy needs no Pisot
+hypothesis.  In Bassino's cubic simple-Parry Pisot family, the quotient gives
+injective apertures $m_n=n-1$ with
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta_n,m_n)=n-1$, so future-only inverse depth is unbounded
+across cubic systems.  The Fibonacci decoder, chamber duality, critical
+Fischer covers, and Markov orders follow as concrete consequences of these
+two collision mechanisms.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}
 \label{sec:intro}
 
-Finite-window recodings can collapse individual input words and still become

-\begin{proof}

-sliding window of length $m$ and outputs one raw bit. Equivalently, the decoder

+\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]
+\label{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}
+Let $\beta$ be an arbitrary quadratic Pisot number and use exactly the
+greedy language, Parry data, rank, cyclic modulus and fold of

 \[

-\subsection{Sharp threshold and extremal bases}

-\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]
-\label{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}
-Let $\beta$ be an arbitrary quadratic Pisot number and use exactly the
-greedy language, Parry data, rank, cyclic modulus and fold of
-Definition~\ref{def:quadratic-parry-fold}.  Then
-\[
-m_*(\beta)=
-\begin{cases}
-3,&\beta\text{ is the root of }x^2-ax-a,\quad a\ge1,\\
-3,&\beta\text{ is the root of }x^2-ax+1,\quad a\ge3,\\
-2,&\text{otherwise}.
-\end{cases}
-\]
-More strongly, for every $m\ge m_*(\beta)$ and every $n\ge m$, the
-finite-block sliding fold is injective and
-\begin{equation}
-|\mathcal L_n(Y_{\beta,m})|
-=(\lfloor\beta\rfloor+1)^{n+m-1}.
-\label{eq:quadratic-pisot-block-count}
-\end{equation}
-At these apertures $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is a topological conjugacy from the full
-$(\lfloor\beta\rfloor+1)$-shift onto the SFT $Y_{\beta,m}$, with inverse of
-memory zero and anticipation $m-1$.
-
-Consequently the maximum of the threshold function on the full quadratic
-Pisot family is three.  Its extremizers are exactly the negative-conjugate

+\section{Finite quadratic arithmetic}
+\label{app:quadratic-arithmetic}
+
+\subsection{The positive-recurrence integer exclusion}
+\label{app:positive-integer-exclusion}
+
+We prove Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.  Put
+\[
+S=a^2+a+b,qquad T=a^3+a^2+2ab+b=aS+b(a+1).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+U_+-a=\frac{b(a+1)}S,qquad L_+-a=\frac{bS}T.
+\]
+For $h=be-ak>0$, divide
+\[
+be=aq+r,qquad qb=ap+t,qquad 0\le r,t<a.
+\]
+Here $0\le q\le b$, and $q\le b-1$ when $r>0$.  If $k\le q-1$, then
+$h\ge a+r$ and
+\[
+hL_+-kb>(a+r)a-(b-1)b\ge a^2-b(b-1)\ge1.
+\]
+The inequality $k\ge q+1$ would give $h<0$.  Hence $k=q$ and $h=r$.
+Writing $j=kb-ah=a(p-r)+t$, the cases $p<r$ and $p>r$ give respectively
+\[
+rL_+-qb=a(r-p)-t+r(L_+-a)>a-t\ge1
+\]
+and
+\[
+qb-rU_+=a(p-r)+t-r(U_+-a)
+>a-\frac{rb}{a}\ge a-b+\frac ba\ge1.
+\]
+
+It remains to treat $p=r$.  Put $w=rb-at$.  The divisions give
+\begin{equation}
+b^2e=r(a^2+b)+at,qquad w=r(a^2+2b)-b^2e.
+\label{eq:app-terminal-divisions}
+\end{equation}
+The integer $w$ cannot vanish.  Indeed, if $a=gA$, $b=gB$ with
+$(A,B)=1$, then $at=rb$ gives $r=AR$, $t=BR$ with $0<R<g$; reduction of
+the first two divisions modulo $g$ and Bezout's identity force $g\mid R$.
+
+Make one further division
+\[
+rb=au+v,qquad 0\le v<a.
+\]
+Then $w=a(u-t)+v$.  Substitution in the three reversed divisions shows
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c}
+\text{sign of }w&\text{quotient relation}&\text{remainder inequality}\\ \hline
+w>0&u-t\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w>0&u-t=1&av\ge b(t+1)\\
+w<0&t-u\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w<0&t-u=1&b(t-1)\ge v(a+1).
+\end{array}
+\]
+For the two boundary rows, substitute $u=t+1$ or $u=t-1$ successively into
+\[
+r=\frac{au+v}{b},\qquad q=\frac{ar+t}{b},\qquad
+e=\frac{aq+r}{b}.
+\]
+After multiplication by $b,b^2,b^3$, failure of the stated remainder
+inequality forces $r\ge a$, $q>b$, or a nonintegral final quotient.  If an
+equality occurs before the last division, write again $a=gA$, $b=gB$; the
+remaining quotient lies strictly between $0$ and $g$, while the three
+divisibilities force it to be divisible by $g$.  This establishes the four
+alternatives without assuming $(a,b)=1$.
+
+Define
+\begin{align*}
+\Delta_L&=rbS-(t+1)T=T\{r(L_+-a)-t-1\},\\
+\Delta_U&=tS-rb(a+1)-S=S\{t-r(U_+-a)-1\}.
+\end{align*}
+Using $T=aS+b(a+1)$ gives
+\[
+\Delta_L=wS-T-tb(a+1),qquad
+\Delta_U=tb+(-w)(a+1)-S.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_L\ge2aS-T-(a-1)b(a+1)=a^2(a-b+1)>0.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t=1$, the remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_L=vS-b(a+1)(t+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$r(L_+-a)-t\ge1$.
+
+If $w<0$ and $t-u\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_U\ge(a+1)^2-S=a+1-b\ge1.
+\]
+If $w<0$ and $t-u=1$, the last remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_U=b(t-1)-v(a+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$t-r(U_+-a)\ge1$.  Since $w\ne0$, one of these alternatives applies and
+proves Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.
+
+\subsection{The aperture-three triple classification}
+\label{app:m3-triples}
+
+For $m=3$, write each congruence in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} as
+\[
+e_t+Q_1e_{t+1}+Q_2e_{t+2}=k_tQ_3,qquad
+k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}.
+\]
+
+In the negative-conjugate chamber,
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a+1,a^2+a+b,a^3+a^2+2ab+b),qquad |e_j|\le a.
+\]
+For one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$, sign symmetry reduces to $k=0,1$.
+When $k=0$, the bound $2Q_2>a(1+Q_1)$ gives $|z|\le1$; $z=0$ gives
+$(x,y)=(0,0)$, and $z=1$ gives $(x,y)=(-b,-a)$.  When $k=1$, the bound
+at $z\le a-1$ forces $z=a$, after which
+$x+(a+1)y=b(a+1)$ gives $(x,y)=(0,b)$.  Hence the solution list is
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(b,a,-1;0),\ \pm(0,b,a;1)\}.
+\]
+Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(a,-1)$, and $\pm(b,a)$.  A final
+triple of type $\pm(0,b,a)$ has initial pair $\pm(0,b)$, which is not a
+terminal pair.  A final triple of type $\pm(b,a,-1)$ forces the preceding
+triple to be $\pm(0,b,a)$, whose initial pair again cannot be terminal.
+
+In the positive-conjugate chamber put $C=a-b$ and $d=a-1$.  Then
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a,a^2-b,a^3-2ab),qquad 2\le C\le d.
+\]
+For $x+ay+Q_2z=kQ_3$, the same bounds give
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(C,d,-1;0),
+\ \pm(-b,C,d;1),\ \pm(C,C-1,d;1)\}.
+\]
+Indeed, for $k=0$ one has $|z|\le1$, and $z=1$ forces
+$(x,y)=(-C,-d)$.  For $k=1$, the inequality at $z\le a-2$ forces $z=d$;
+reducing $x+ay=aC-b$ modulo $a$ leaves precisely
+$(x,y)=(-b,C)$ and $(C,C-1)$.  The terminal pairs are
+$(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and $\pm(C-1,d)$.  Neither
+$\pm(-b,C)$ nor $\pm(C,C-1)$ is terminal.  The remaining type
+$\pm(C,d,-1)$ forces a preceding $\pm(-b,C,d)$, whose initial pair is not
+terminal.
+
+Thus, in either chamber, a nonzero triple cannot persist through all three
+overlaps.  Reading the three equations backwards forces
+$e_2=e_3=e_4=0$, then $e_1=0$, and finally $e_0=0$.

 \begin{abstract}
-We determine exact overlap thresholds and local inverse structure for cyclic
-language-rank recodings of quadratic and simple-Parry beta-languages.  A
-legal length-$m$ word is identified with its colexicographic positional rank;
-the same rank is evaluated on the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number
-of legal words, returned to the legal language, and overlapped along the

-$\beta$-normalization.

+\section{Finite quadratic arithmetic}
+\label{app:quadratic-arithmetic}
+
+\subsection{The positive-recurrence integer exclusion}
+\label{app:positive-integer-exclusion}
+
+We prove Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.  Put
+\[
+S=a^2+a+b,qquad T=a^3+a^2+2ab+b=aS+b(a+1).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+U_+-a=\frac{b(a+1)}S,qquad L_+-a=\frac{bS}T.
+\]
+For $h=be-ak>0$, divide
+\[
+be=aq+r,qquad qb=ap+t,qquad 0\le r,t<a.
+\]
+Here $0\le q\le b$, and $q\le b-1$ when $r>0$.  If $k\le q-1$, then
+$h\ge a+r$ and
+\[
+hL_+-kb>(a+r)a-(b-1)b\ge a^2-b(b-1)\ge1.
+\]
+The inequality $k\ge q+1$ would give $h<0$.  Hence $k=q$ and $h=r$.
+Writing $j=kb-ah=a(p-r)+t$, the cases $p<r$ and $p>r$ give respectively
+\[
+rL_+-qb=a(r-p)-t+r(L_+-a)>a-t\ge1
+\]
+and
+\[
+qb-rU_+=a(p-r)+t-r(U_+-a)
+>a-\frac{rb}{a}\ge a-b+\frac ba\ge1.
+\]
+
+It remains to treat $p=r$.  Put $w=rb-at$.  The divisions give
+\begin{equation}
+b^2e=r(a^2+b)+at,qquad w=r(a^2+2b)-b^2e.
+\label{eq:app-terminal-divisions}
+\end{equation}
+The integer $w$ cannot vanish.  Indeed, if $a=gA$, $b=gB$ with
+$(A,B)=1$, then $at=rb$ gives $r=AR$, $t=BR$ with $0<R<g$; reduction of
+the first two divisions modulo $g$ and Bezout's identity force $g\mid R$.
+
+Make one further division
+\[
+rb=au+v,qquad 0\le v<a.
+\]
+Then $w=a(u-t)+v$.  Substitution in the three reversed divisions shows
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c}
+\text{sign of }w&\text{quotient relation}&\text{remainder inequality}\\ \hline
+w>0&u-t\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w>0&u-t=1&av\ge b(t+1)\\
+w<0&t-u\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w<0&t-u=1&b(t-1)\ge v(a+1).
+\end{array}
+\]
+For the two boundary rows, substitute $u=t+1$ or $u=t-1$ successively into
+\[
+r=\frac{au+v}{b},\qquad q=\frac{ar+t}{b},\qquad
+e=\frac{aq+r}{b}.
+\]
+After multiplication by $b,b^2,b^3$, failure of the stated remainder
+inequality forces $r\ge a$, $q>b$, or a nonintegral final quotient.  If an
+equality occurs before the last division, write again $a=gA$, $b=gB$; the
+remaining quotient lies strictly between $0$ and $g$, while the three
+divisibilities force it to be divisible by $g$.  This establishes the four
+alternatives without assuming $(a,b)=1$.
+
+Define
+\begin{align*}
+\Delta_L&=rbS-(t+1)T=T\{r(L_+-a)-t-1\},\\
+\Delta_U&=tS-rb(a+1)-S=S\{t-r(U_+-a)-1\}.
+\end{align*}
+Using $T=aS+b(a+1)$ gives
+\[
+\Delta_L=wS-T-tb(a+1),qquad
+\Delta_U=tb+(-w)(a+1)-S.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_L\ge2aS-T-(a-1)b(a+1)=a^2(a-b+1)>0.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t=1$, the remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_L=vS-b(a+1)(t+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$r(L_+-a)-t\ge1$.
+
+If $w<0$ and $t-u\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_U\ge(a+1)^2-S=a+1-b\ge1.
+\]
+If $w<0$ and $t-u=1$, the last remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_U=b(t-1)-v(a+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$t-r(U_+-a)\ge1$.  Since $w\ne0$, one of these alternatives applies and
+proves Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.
+
+\subsection{The aperture-three triple classification}
+\label{app:m3-triples}
+
+For $m=3$, write each congruence in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} as
+\[
+e_t+Q_1e_{t+1}+Q_2e_{t+2}=k_tQ_3,qquad
+k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}.
+\]
+
+In the negative-conjugate chamber,
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a+1,a^2+a+b,a^3+a^2+2ab+b),qquad |e_j|\le a.
+\]
+For one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$, sign symmetry reduces to $k=0,1$.
+When $k=0$, the bound $2Q_2>a(1+Q_1)$ gives $|z|\le1$; $z=0$ gives
+$(x,y)=(0,0)$, and $z=1$ gives $(x,y)=(-b,-a)$.  When $k=1$, the bound
+at $z\le a-1$ forces $z=a$, after which
+$x+(a+1)y=b(a+1)$ gives $(x,y)=(0,b)$.  Hence the solution list is
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(b,a,-1;0),\ \pm(0,b,a;1)\}.
+\]
+Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(a,-1)$, and $\pm(b,a)$.  A final
+triple of type $\pm(0,b,a)$ has initial pair $\pm(0,b)$, which is not a
+terminal pair.  A final triple of type $\pm(b,a,-1)$ forces the preceding
+triple to be $\pm(0,b,a)$, whose initial pair again cannot be terminal.
+
+In the positive-conjugate chamber put $C=a-b$ and $d=a-1$.  Then
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a,a^2-b,a^3-2ab),qquad 2\le C\le d.
+\]
+For $x+ay+Q_2z=kQ_3$, the same bounds give
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(C,d,-1;0),
+\ \pm(-b,C,d;1),\ \pm(C,C-1,d;1)\}.
+\]
+Indeed, for $k=0$ one has $|z|\le1$, and $z=1$ forces
+$(x,y)=(-C,-d)$.  For $k=1$, the inequality at $z\le a-2$ forces $z=d$;
+reducing $x+ay=aC-b$ modulo $a$ leaves precisely
+$(x,y)=(-b,C)$ and $(C,C-1)$.  The terminal pairs are
+$(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and $\pm(C-1,d)$.  Neither
+$\pm(-b,C)$ nor $\pm(C,C-1)$ is terminal.  The remaining type
+$\pm(C,d,-1)$ forces a preceding $\pm(-b,C,d)$, whose initial pair is not
+terminal.
+
+Thus, in either chamber, a nonzero triple cannot persist through all three
+overlaps.  Reading the three equations backwards forces
+$e_2=e_3=e_4=0$, then $e_1=0$, and finally $e_0=0$.

 \begin{abstract}
-We determine exact overlap thresholds and local inverse structure for cyclic
-language-rank recodings of quadratic and simple-Parry beta-languages.  A
-legal length-$m$ word is identified with its colexicographic positional rank;
-the same rank is evaluated on the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number
-of legal words, returned to the legal language, and overlapped along the
-shift.  This is cyclic reduction of integer language ranks, not numerical
-$\beta$-normalization.
-

-Markov order in the stabilized alphabet.  The metallic family becomes a
-transparent specialization of this classification.

 \begin{remark}\label{rem:sofic-comparison}
-In the terminology of \cite{LindMarcus1995}, $\mathcal G_m$ is a
-right-resolving presentation of the sofic shift $Y_m$, and $\Phi_m$ has degree
-at most $2^{m-1}$ by the finite-state lift above. A right-resolving
-factor of degree~1 between irreducible shifts of finite type is a conjugacy
-\cite[Theorem~8.1.16]{LindMarcus1995}; see also \cite{Ashley1991} for the
-equal-entropy resolving theory and \cite{Boyle1983} for the lower-entropy
-obstruction. The threshold theorem says that degree~1 is achieved exactly at

-framework, and it uses the explicit decoder of Lemma~\ref{lem:m3-decoder}.
+The graph $\mathcal G_m$ is a bi-resolving presentation of $Y_m$ with degree
+at most $2^{m-1}$.  General resolving-map theory supplies this framework
+\cite{LindMarcus1995,Ashley1991,Boyle1983}; the degree-one threshold is the
+arithmetic content of Lemma~\ref{lem:m3-decoder} and Theorem

+\eqref{eq:cubic-unbounded-polynomial} and put $m_n=n-1$.  Then $\beta_n$
+is a nonintegral cubic simple-Parry Pisot number, $\Phi_{\beta_n,m_n}$ is
+injective, and
+\begin{equation}

+\label{eq:cubic-unbounded-causal-length}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently
+\[

+\substack{\beta\text{ nonintegral cubic simple-Parry Pisot},\\
+m\ge2,\ \Phi_{\beta,m}\text{ injective}}\right\}=\infty.
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+

+forces the second carry to vanish uniformly, and Lemma
+\ref{lem:cubic-unbounded-terminal-paths} identifies the last two nonzero
+paths and shows that one more output eliminates them.

+\section{Finite quadratic arithmetic}
+\label{app:quadratic-arithmetic}
+
+\subsection{The positive-recurrence integer exclusion}
+\label{app:positive-integer-exclusion}
+
+We prove Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.  Put
+\[
+S=a^2+a+b,qquad T=a^3+a^2+2ab+b=aS+b(a+1).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+U_+-a=\frac{b(a+1)}S,qquad L_+-a=\frac{bS}T.
+\]
+For $h=be-ak>0$, divide
+\[
+be=aq+r,qquad qb=ap+t,qquad 0\le r,t<a.
+\]
+Here $0\le q\le b$, and $q\le b-1$ when $r>0$.  If $k\le q-1$, then
+$h\ge a+r$ and
+\[
+hL_+-kb>(a+r)a-(b-1)b\ge a^2-b(b-1)\ge1.
+\]
+The inequality $k\ge q+1$ would give $h<0$.  Hence $k=q$ and $h=r$.
+Writing $j=kb-ah=a(p-r)+t$, the cases $p<r$ and $p>r$ give respectively
+\[
+rL_+-qb=a(r-p)-t+r(L_+-a)>a-t\ge1
+\]
+and
+\[
+qb-rU_+=a(p-r)+t-r(U_+-a)
+>a-\frac{rb}{a}\ge a-b+\frac ba\ge1.
+\]
+
+It remains to treat $p=r$.  Put $w=rb-at$.  The divisions give
+\begin{equation}
+b^2e=r(a^2+b)+at,qquad w=r(a^2+2b)-b^2e.
+\label{eq:app-terminal-divisions}
+\end{equation}
+The integer $w$ cannot vanish.  Indeed, if $a=gA$, $b=gB$ with
+$(A,B)=1$, then $at=rb$ gives $r=AR$, $t=BR$ with $0<R<g$; reduction of
+the first two divisions modulo $g$ and Bezout's identity force $g\mid R$.
+
+Make one further division
+\[
+rb=au+v,qquad 0\le v<a.
+\]
+Then $w=a(u-t)+v$.  Substitution in the three reversed divisions shows
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c}
+\text{sign of }w&\text{quotient relation}&\text{remainder inequality}\\ \hline
+w>0&u-t\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w>0&u-t=1&av\ge b(t+1)\\
+w<0&t-u\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w<0&t-u=1&b(t-1)\ge v(a+1).
+\end{array}
+\]
+For the two boundary rows, substitute $u=t+1$ or $u=t-1$ successively into
+\[
+r=\frac{au+v}{b},\qquad q=\frac{ar+t}{b},\qquad
+e=\frac{aq+r}{b}.
+\]
+After multiplication by $b,b^2,b^3$, failure of the stated remainder
+inequality forces $r\ge a$, $q>b$, or a nonintegral final quotient.  If an
+equality occurs before the last division, write again $a=gA$, $b=gB$; the
+remaining quotient lies strictly between $0$ and $g$, while the three
+divisibilities force it to be divisible by $g$.  This establishes the four
+alternatives without assuming $(a,b)=1$.
+
+Define
+\begin{align*}
+\Delta_L&=rbS-(t+1)T=T\{r(L_+-a)-t-1\},\\
+\Delta_U&=tS-rb(a+1)-S=S\{t-r(U_+-a)-1\}.
+\end{align*}
+Using $T=aS+b(a+1)$ gives
+\[
+\Delta_L=wS-T-tb(a+1),qquad
+\Delta_U=tb+(-w)(a+1)-S.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_L\ge2aS-T-(a-1)b(a+1)=a^2(a-b+1)>0.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t=1$, the remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_L=vS-b(a+1)(t+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$r(L_+-a)-t\ge1$.
+
+If $w<0$ and $t-u\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_U\ge(a+1)^2-S=a+1-b\ge1.
+\]
+If $w<0$ and $t-u=1$, the last remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_U=b(t-1)-v(a+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$t-r(U_+-a)\ge1$.  Since $w\ne0$, one of these alternatives applies and
+proves Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.

+\subsection{The aperture-three triple classification}
+\label{app:m3-triples}
+
+For $m=3$, write each congruence in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} as
+\[
+e_t+Q_1e_{t+1}+Q_2e_{t+2}=k_tQ_3,qquad
+k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}.
+\]
+
+In the negative-conjugate chamber,
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a+1,a^2+a+b,a^3+a^2+2ab+b),qquad |e_j|\le a.
+\]
+For one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$, sign symmetry reduces to $k=0,1$.
+When $k=0$, the bound $2Q_2>a(1+Q_1)$ gives $|z|\le1$; $z=0$ gives
+$(x,y)=(0,0)$, and $z=1$ gives $(x,y)=(-b,-a)$.  When $k=1$, the bound
+at $z\le a-1$ forces $z=a$, after which
+$x+(a+1)y=b(a+1)$ gives $(x,y)=(0,b)$.  Hence the solution list is
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(b,a,-1;0),\ \pm(0,b,a;1)\}.
+\]
+Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(a,-1)$, and $\pm(b,a)$.  A final
+triple of type $\pm(0,b,a)$ has initial pair $\pm(0,b)$, which is not a
+terminal pair.  A final triple of type $\pm(b,a,-1)$ forces the preceding
+triple to be $\pm(0,b,a)$, whose initial pair again cannot be terminal.
+
+In the positive-conjugate chamber put $C=a-b$ and $d=a-1$.  Then
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a,a^2-b,a^3-2ab),qquad 2\le C\le d.
+\]
+For $x+ay+Q_2z=kQ_3$, the same bounds give
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(C,d,-1;0),
+\ \pm(-b,C,d;1),\ \pm(C,C-1,d;1)\}.
+\]
+Indeed, for $k=0$ one has $|z|\le1$, and $z=1$ forces
+$(x,y)=(-C,-d)$.  For $k=1$, the inequality at $z\le a-2$ forces $z=d$;
+reducing $x+ay=aC-b$ modulo $a$ leaves precisely
+$(x,y)=(-b,C)$ and $(C,C-1)$.  The terminal pairs are
+$(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and $\pm(C-1,d)$.  Neither
+$\pm(-b,C)$ nor $\pm(C,C-1)$ is terminal.  The remaining type
+$\pm(C,d,-1)$ forces a preceding $\pm(-b,C,d)$, whose initial pair is not
+terminal.
+
+Thus, in either chamber, a nonzero triple cannot persist through all three
+overlaps.  Reading the three equations backwards forces
+$e_2=e_3=e_4=0$, then $e_1=0$, and finally $e_0=0$.

 \begin{abstract}
-We determine exact overlap thresholds and local inverse structure for cyclic
-language-rank recodings of quadratic and simple-Parry beta-languages.  A
-legal length-$m$ word is identified with its colexicographic positional rank;
-the same rank is evaluated on the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number
-of legal words, returned to the legal language, and overlapped along the
-shift.  This is cyclic reduction of integer language ranks, not numerical
-$\beta$-normalization.
-
-The Fibonacci model has sharp nontrivial threshold three.  We give its
-explicit three-window decoder, low-window counterexamples, and complete
-two-window branch locus.  For every quadratic Pisot base, the least
-nontrivial aperture is three exactly for the roots of
-$x^2-ax-a$ and $x^2-ax+1$, and is two otherwise.  We also determine chamber
-duality, future-only inverse bounds, the critical two-fixed-point normal
-form, exact finite-block onset, the canonical right Fischer cover, and exact
-Markov order in the stabilized alphabet.  The metallic family becomes a
-transparent specialization of this classification.
+We study sliding recodings obtained by reducing colexicographic language
+ranks modulo the number of legal words and overlapping the resulting finite
+windows.  For every quadratic Pisot $\beta$-language, the least nontrivial
+injective aperture is three precisely for the roots of $x^2-ax-a$ and
+$x^2-ax+1$, and is two otherwise.  The future-only inverse length is three in
+the positive-conjugate chamber and two in the negative chamber at aperture
+three; for negative conjugate and aperture $m\ge4$ we prove the bounds
+$2\le\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)\le m$.
 
 For every nonintegral simple-Parry base, a coordinatewise-difference quotient
-of the classical pair graph preserves every collision and gives an exact
-longest-path formula for future-only inverse depth.  We derive the complete
-aperture-two trichotomy without a Pisot hypothesis.  Applied to Bassino's
-cubic simple-Parry Pisot family, the quotient gives injective apertures
-$m_n=n-1$ with exact future-only inverse length $n-1$, hence unbounded depth
-across the family.
+of the classical pair graph preserves all collisions.  Its longest directed
+paths give the future-only inverse length, while reachable cycles decide
+noninjectivity; the resulting aperture-two trichotomy needs no Pisot
+hypothesis.  In Bassino's cubic simple-Parry Pisot family, the quotient gives
+injective apertures $m_n=n-1$ with
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta_n,m_n)=n-1$, so future-only inverse depth is unbounded
+across cubic systems.  The Fibonacci decoder, chamber duality, critical
+Fischer covers, and Markov orders follow as concrete consequences of these
+two collision mechanisms.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}
 \label{sec:intro}
 
-Finite-window recodings can collapse individual input words and still become
-invertible when their outputs are overlapped.  This paper determines where
-that transition occurs, how much future output a memory-zero inverse needs,

-Assume $m\ge3$.  Then:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
-  \item The factor map
-  \[
-  \Phi_m:(\{0,1\}^{\ZZ},\sigma)\longrightarrow(Y_m,\sigma)
-  \]
-  is a topological conjugacy.  Its inverse is
-  \[
-  \Phi_m^{-1}(y)_t=\psi_m(y_t,\ldots,y_{t+m-1}).
-  \]
-  \item Let $\mathcal B_m:=\mathcal L_m(Y_m)$ and, for
-  $W\in\mathcal B_m$, let $\Psi_{m,m}(W)\in\{0,1\}^{2m-1}$ be the unique
-  raw block with $\Phi_{m,m}(\Psi_{m,m}(W))=W$.  A sequence
-  $y\in(X_m)^{\ZZ}$ belongs to $Y_m$ if and only if every length-$m$ block
-  $W_t:=(y_t,\ldots,y_{t+m-1})$ lies in $\mathcal B_m$ and the decoded raw
-  blocks satisfy the overlap condition
-  \[
-  \Psi_{m,m}(W_t)_{1,\ldots,2m-2}
-  =
-  \Psi_{m,m}(W_{t+1})_{0,\ldots,2m-3}
-  \qquad\text{for all }t\in\ZZ.
-  \]
-  \item In particular $Y_m$ is a subshift of finite type.  It is defined by
-  finitely many forbidden words of length at most $m+1$ over the alphabet
-  $X_m$.
-  \item Pushforward by $\Phi_m$ gives a bijection between shift-invariant
-  Borel probability measures on $\{0,1\}^{\ZZ}$ and shift-invariant Borel
-  probability measures on $Y_m$, with inverse pushforward by the displayed
-  local decoder.
-\end{enumerate}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The explicit decoder in Section~\ref{sec:stab:conjugacy} gives a continuous
-shift-commuting left inverse to $\Phi_m$ on $Y_m$.  Since $Y_m$ is the image of
-$\Phi_m$, this left inverse is also a right inverse on $Y_m$.  Hence $\Phi_m$
-is a topological conjugacy, proving (i).
-
-If $y=\Phi_m(a)$, then each $W_t$ lies in $\mathcal B_m$ and
-$\Psi_{m,m}(W_t)=a_ta_{t+1}\ldots a_{t+2m-2}$.  Consecutive decoded raw
-blocks therefore overlap in their common $2m-2$ coordinates, so the condition
-in (ii) is necessary.
-
-Conversely, suppose a sequence $y\in(X_m)^{\ZZ}$ satisfies the two conditions
-in (ii).  The overlap condition glues the finite words
-$\Psi_{m,m}(W_t)$ into a unique bi-infinite binary sequence $a$ such that
-\[
-\Psi_{m,m}(W_t)=a_ta_{t+1}\ldots a_{t+2m-2}
-\qquad\text{for all }t.
-\]
-Applying $\Phi_{m,m}$ to this raw block gives $W_t$, so in particular
-\[
-\Fold_m(a_t,\ldots,a_{t+m-1})=y_t
-\]
-for every $t$.  Thus $y=\Phi_m(a)\in Y_m$.  This proves (ii).
-
-The criterion in (ii) depends only on adjacent length-$m$ output blocks, hence
-only on words of length $m+1$ over the finite alphabet $X_m$.  There are
-finitely many violations, so $Y_m$ is an SFT with memory at most $m$.  This
-proves (iii).
-
-Finally, a topological conjugacy sends invariant Borel probability measures
-bijectively to invariant Borel probability measures by pushforward, and the
-inverse bijection is pushforward by the inverse conjugacy.  The inverse
-conjugacy is the local decoder in (i), proving (iv).
-\end{proof}

-\begin{remark}[Decoder complexity]\label{rem:decoder-complexity}
-The inverse code supplied above reads a
-sliding window of length $m$ and outputs one raw bit. Equivalently, the decoder
-may be implemented by maintaining an overlap state of size $m-1$. The
-arithmetic cost is $O(m)$ per output symbol, since each decoding step involves
-at most $m$ Fibonacci-weighted additions modulo $F_{m+2}$.
-\end{remark}

 \begin{remark}\label{rem:sofic-comparison}
-In the terminology of \cite{LindMarcus1995}, $\mathcal G_m$ is a
-right-resolving presentation of the sofic shift $Y_m$, and $\Phi_m$ has degree
-at most $2^{m-1}$ by the finite-state lift above. A right-resolving
-factor of degree~1 between irreducible shifts of finite type is a conjugacy
-\cite[Theorem~8.1.16]{LindMarcus1995}; see also \cite{Ashley1991} for the
-equal-entropy resolving theory and \cite{Boyle1983} for the lower-entropy
-obstruction. The threshold theorem says that degree~1 is achieved exactly at

-framework, and it uses the explicit decoder of Lemma~\ref{lem:m3-decoder}.
+The graph $\mathcal G_m$ is a bi-resolving presentation of $Y_m$ with degree
+at most $2^{m-1}$.  General resolving-map theory supplies this framework
+\cite{LindMarcus1995,Ashley1991,Boyle1983}; the degree-one threshold is the
+arithmetic content of Lemma~\ref{lem:m3-decoder} and Theorem

 \end{remark}

+\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]
+\label{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}
+Let $\beta$ be an arbitrary quadratic Pisot number and use exactly the
+greedy language, Parry data, rank, cyclic modulus and fold of

 \[

-\subsection{Sharp threshold and extremal bases}

-\begin{theorem}[Exact quadratic-Pisot threshold]
-\label{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}
-Let $\beta$ be an arbitrary quadratic Pisot number and use exactly the
-greedy language, Parry data, rank, cyclic modulus and fold of
-Definition~\ref{def:quadratic-parry-fold}.  Then
-\[
-m_*(\beta)=
-\begin{cases}
-3,&\beta\text{ is the root of }x^2-ax-a,\quad a\ge1,\\
-3,&\beta\text{ is the root of }x^2-ax+1,\quad a\ge3,\\
-2,&\text{otherwise}.
-\end{cases}
-\]
-More strongly, for every $m\ge m_*(\beta)$ and every $n\ge m$, the
-finite-block sliding fold is injective and
-\begin{equation}
-|\mathcal L_n(Y_{\beta,m})|
-=(\lfloor\beta\rfloor+1)^{n+m-1}.
-\label{eq:quadratic-pisot-block-count}
-\end{equation}
-At these apertures $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is a topological conjugacy from the full
-$(\lfloor\beta\rfloor+1)$-shift onto the SFT $Y_{\beta,m}$, with inverse of
-memory zero and anticipation $m-1$.
-
-Consequently the maximum of the threshold function on the full quadratic
-Pisot family is three.  Its extremizers are exactly the negative-conjugate

+\section{Finite quadratic arithmetic}
+\label{app:quadratic-arithmetic}
+
+\subsection{The positive-recurrence integer exclusion}
+\label{app:positive-integer-exclusion}
+
+We prove Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.  Put
+\[
+S=a^2+a+b,qquad T=a^3+a^2+2ab+b=aS+b(a+1).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+U_+-a=\frac{b(a+1)}S,qquad L_+-a=\frac{bS}T.
+\]
+For $h=be-ak>0$, divide
+\[
+be=aq+r,qquad qb=ap+t,qquad 0\le r,t<a.
+\]
+Here $0\le q\le b$, and $q\le b-1$ when $r>0$.  If $k\le q-1$, then
+$h\ge a+r$ and
+\[
+hL_+-kb>(a+r)a-(b-1)b\ge a^2-b(b-1)\ge1.
+\]
+The inequality $k\ge q+1$ would give $h<0$.  Hence $k=q$ and $h=r$.
+Writing $j=kb-ah=a(p-r)+t$, the cases $p<r$ and $p>r$ give respectively
+\[
+rL_+-qb=a(r-p)-t+r(L_+-a)>a-t\ge1
+\]
+and
+\[
+qb-rU_+=a(p-r)+t-r(U_+-a)
+>a-\frac{rb}{a}\ge a-b+\frac ba\ge1.
+\]
+
+It remains to treat $p=r$.  Put $w=rb-at$.  The divisions give
+\begin{equation}
+b^2e=r(a^2+b)+at,qquad w=r(a^2+2b)-b^2e.
+\label{eq:app-terminal-divisions}
+\end{equation}
+The integer $w$ cannot vanish.  Indeed, if $a=gA$, $b=gB$ with
+$(A,B)=1$, then $at=rb$ gives $r=AR$, $t=BR$ with $0<R<g$; reduction of
+the first two divisions modulo $g$ and Bezout's identity force $g\mid R$.
+
+Make one further division
+\[
+rb=au+v,qquad 0\le v<a.
+\]
+Then $w=a(u-t)+v$.  Substitution in the three reversed divisions shows
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c}
+\text{sign of }w&\text{quotient relation}&\text{remainder inequality}\\ \hline
+w>0&u-t\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w>0&u-t=1&av\ge b(t+1)\\
+w<0&t-u\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w<0&t-u=1&b(t-1)\ge v(a+1).
+\end{array}
+\]
+For the two boundary rows, substitute $u=t+1$ or $u=t-1$ successively into
+\[
+r=\frac{au+v}{b},\qquad q=\frac{ar+t}{b},\qquad
+e=\frac{aq+r}{b}.
+\]
+After multiplication by $b,b^2,b^3$, failure of the stated remainder
+inequality forces $r\ge a$, $q>b$, or a nonintegral final quotient.  If an
+equality occurs before the last division, write again $a=gA$, $b=gB$; the
+remaining quotient lies strictly between $0$ and $g$, while the three
+divisibilities force it to be divisible by $g$.  This establishes the four
+alternatives without assuming $(a,b)=1$.
+
+Define
+\begin{align*}
+\Delta_L&=rbS-(t+1)T=T\{r(L_+-a)-t-1\},\\
+\Delta_U&=tS-rb(a+1)-S=S\{t-r(U_+-a)-1\}.
+\end{align*}
+Using $T=aS+b(a+1)$ gives
+\[
+\Delta_L=wS-T-tb(a+1),qquad
+\Delta_U=tb+(-w)(a+1)-S.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_L\ge2aS-T-(a-1)b(a+1)=a^2(a-b+1)>0.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t=1$, the remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_L=vS-b(a+1)(t+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$r(L_+-a)-t\ge1$.
+
+If $w<0$ and $t-u\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_U\ge(a+1)^2-S=a+1-b\ge1.
+\]
+If $w<0$ and $t-u=1$, the last remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_U=b(t-1)-v(a+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$t-r(U_+-a)\ge1$.  Since $w\ne0$, one of these alternatives applies and
+proves Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.
+
+\subsection{The aperture-three triple classification}
+\label{app:m3-triples}
+
+For $m=3$, write each congruence in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} as
+\[
+e_t+Q_1e_{t+1}+Q_2e_{t+2}=k_tQ_3,qquad
+k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}.
+\]
+
+In the negative-conjugate chamber,
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a+1,a^2+a+b,a^3+a^2+2ab+b),qquad |e_j|\le a.
+\]
+For one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$, sign symmetry reduces to $k=0,1$.
+When $k=0$, the bound $2Q_2>a(1+Q_1)$ gives $|z|\le1$; $z=0$ gives
+$(x,y)=(0,0)$, and $z=1$ gives $(x,y)=(-b,-a)$.  When $k=1$, the bound
+at $z\le a-1$ forces $z=a$, after which
+$x+(a+1)y=b(a+1)$ gives $(x,y)=(0,b)$.  Hence the solution list is
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(b,a,-1;0),\ \pm(0,b,a;1)\}.
+\]
+Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(a,-1)$, and $\pm(b,a)$.  A final
+triple of type $\pm(0,b,a)$ has initial pair $\pm(0,b)$, which is not a
+terminal pair.  A final triple of type $\pm(b,a,-1)$ forces the preceding
+triple to be $\pm(0,b,a)$, whose initial pair again cannot be terminal.
+
+In the positive-conjugate chamber put $C=a-b$ and $d=a-1$.  Then
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a,a^2-b,a^3-2ab),qquad 2\le C\le d.
+\]
+For $x+ay+Q_2z=kQ_3$, the same bounds give
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(C,d,-1;0),
+\ \pm(-b,C,d;1),\ \pm(C,C-1,d;1)\}.
+\]
+Indeed, for $k=0$ one has $|z|\le1$, and $z=1$ forces
+$(x,y)=(-C,-d)$.  For $k=1$, the inequality at $z\le a-2$ forces $z=d$;
+reducing $x+ay=aC-b$ modulo $a$ leaves precisely
+$(x,y)=(-b,C)$ and $(C,C-1)$.  The terminal pairs are
+$(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and $\pm(C-1,d)$.  Neither
+$\pm(-b,C)$ nor $\pm(C,C-1)$ is terminal.  The remaining type
+$\pm(C,d,-1)$ forces a preceding $\pm(-b,C,d)$, whose initial pair is not
+terminal.
+
+Thus, in either chamber, a nonzero triple cannot persist through all three
+overlaps.  Reading the three equations backwards forces
+$e_2=e_3=e_4=0$, then $e_1=0$, and finally $e_0=0$.

-We determine exact overlap thresholds and local inverse structure for cyclic

+For $n\ge4$, let $\beta_n\in(n,n+1)$ be the root of
+\eqref{eq:cubic-unbounded-polynomial} and put $m_n=n-1$.  Then $\beta_n$
+is a nonintegral cubic simple-Parry Pisot number, $\Phi_{\beta_n,m_n}$ is
+injective, and
+\begin{equation}
+\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta_n,m_n)=n-1.
+\label{eq:cubic-unbounded-causal-length}
+\end{equation}
+Consequently
+\[
+\sup\left\{\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m):
+\substack{\beta\text{ nonintegral cubic simple-Parry Pisot},\\
+m\ge2,\ \Phi_{\beta,m}\text{ injective}}\right\}=\infty.
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+
+The proof reduces to two facts.  Lemma~\ref{lem:cubic-unbounded-two-window}
+forces the second carry to vanish uniformly, and Lemma
+\ref{lem:cubic-unbounded-terminal-paths} identifies the last two nonzero
+paths and shows that one more output eliminates them.

+\section{Finite quadratic arithmetic}
+\label{app:quadratic-arithmetic}
+
+\subsection{The positive-recurrence integer exclusion}
+\label{app:positive-integer-exclusion}
+
+We prove Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.  Put
+\[
+S=a^2+a+b,qquad T=a^3+a^2+2ab+b=aS+b(a+1).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+U_+-a=\frac{b(a+1)}S,qquad L_+-a=\frac{bS}T.
+\]
+For $h=be-ak>0$, divide
+\[
+be=aq+r,qquad qb=ap+t,qquad 0\le r,t<a.
+\]
+Here $0\le q\le b$, and $q\le b-1$ when $r>0$.  If $k\le q-1$, then
+$h\ge a+r$ and
+\[
+hL_+-kb>(a+r)a-(b-1)b\ge a^2-b(b-1)\ge1.
+\]
+The inequality $k\ge q+1$ would give $h<0$.  Hence $k=q$ and $h=r$.
+Writing $j=kb-ah=a(p-r)+t$, the cases $p<r$ and $p>r$ give respectively
+\[
+rL_+-qb=a(r-p)-t+r(L_+-a)>a-t\ge1
+\]
+and
+\[
+qb-rU_+=a(p-r)+t-r(U_+-a)
+>a-\frac{rb}{a}\ge a-b+\frac ba\ge1.
+\]
+
+It remains to treat $p=r$.  Put $w=rb-at$.  The divisions give
+\begin{equation}
+b^2e=r(a^2+b)+at,qquad w=r(a^2+2b)-b^2e.
+\label{eq:app-terminal-divisions}
+\end{equation}
+The integer $w$ cannot vanish.  Indeed, if $a=gA$, $b=gB$ with
+$(A,B)=1$, then $at=rb$ gives $r=AR$, $t=BR$ with $0<R<g$; reduction of
+the first two divisions modulo $g$ and Bezout's identity force $g\mid R$.
+
+Make one further division
+\[
+rb=au+v,qquad 0\le v<a.
+\]
+Then $w=a(u-t)+v$.  Substitution in the three reversed divisions shows
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c}
+\text{sign of }w&\text{quotient relation}&\text{remainder inequality}\\ \hline
+w>0&u-t\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w>0&u-t=1&av\ge b(t+1)\\
+w<0&t-u\ge2&\text{automatic}\\
+w<0&t-u=1&b(t-1)\ge v(a+1).
+\end{array}
+\]
+For the two boundary rows, substitute $u=t+1$ or $u=t-1$ successively into
+\[
+r=\frac{au+v}{b},\qquad q=\frac{ar+t}{b},\qquad
+e=\frac{aq+r}{b}.
+\]
+After multiplication by $b,b^2,b^3$, failure of the stated remainder
+inequality forces $r\ge a$, $q>b$, or a nonintegral final quotient.  If an
+equality occurs before the last division, write again $a=gA$, $b=gB$; the
+remaining quotient lies strictly between $0$ and $g$, while the three
+divisibilities force it to be divisible by $g$.  This establishes the four
+alternatives without assuming $(a,b)=1$.
+
+Define
+\begin{align*}
+\Delta_L&=rbS-(t+1)T=T\{r(L_+-a)-t-1\},\\
+\Delta_U&=tS-rb(a+1)-S=S\{t-r(U_+-a)-1\}.
+\end{align*}
+Using $T=aS+b(a+1)$ gives
+\[
+\Delta_L=wS-T-tb(a+1),qquad
+\Delta_U=tb+(-w)(a+1)-S.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_L\ge2aS-T-(a-1)b(a+1)=a^2(a-b+1)>0.
+\]
+If $w>0$ and $u-t=1$, the remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_L=vS-b(a+1)(t+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$r(L_+-a)-t\ge1$.
+
+If $w<0$ and $t-u\ge2$, then
+\[
+\Delta_U\ge(a+1)^2-S=a+1-b\ge1.
+\]
+If $w<0$ and $t-u=1$, the last remainder inequality gives
+$\Delta_U=b(t-1)-v(a+1)\ge0$.  Thus
+$t-r(U_+-a)\ge1$.  Since $w\ne0$, one of these alternatives applies and
+proves Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-integer-exclusion}.
+
+\subsection{The aperture-three triple classification}
+\label{app:m3-triples}
+
+For $m=3$, write each congruence in \eqref{eq:sliding-kernel} as
+\[
+e_t+Q_1e_{t+1}+Q_2e_{t+2}=k_tQ_3,qquad
+k_t\in\{-1,0,1\}.
+\]
+
+In the negative-conjugate chamber,
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a+1,a^2+a+b,a^3+a^2+2ab+b),qquad |e_j|\le a.
+\]
+For one equation $x+Q_1y+Q_2z=kQ_3$, sign symmetry reduces to $k=0,1$.
+When $k=0$, the bound $2Q_2>a(1+Q_1)$ gives $|z|\le1$; $z=0$ gives
+$(x,y)=(0,0)$, and $z=1$ gives $(x,y)=(-b,-a)$.  When $k=1$, the bound
+at $z\le a-1$ forces $z=a$, after which
+$x+(a+1)y=b(a+1)$ gives $(x,y)=(0,b)$.  Hence the solution list is
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(b,a,-1;0),\ \pm(0,b,a;1)\}.
+\]
+Its terminal pairs are $(0,0)$, $\pm(a,-1)$, and $\pm(b,a)$.  A final
+triple of type $\pm(0,b,a)$ has initial pair $\pm(0,b)$, which is not a
+terminal pair.  A final triple of type $\pm(b,a,-1)$ forces the preceding
+triple to be $\pm(0,b,a)$, whose initial pair again cannot be terminal.
+
+In the positive-conjugate chamber put $C=a-b$ and $d=a-1$.  Then
+\[
+(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3)=(a,a^2-b,a^3-2ab),qquad 2\le C\le d.
+\]
+For $x+ay+Q_2z=kQ_3$, the same bounds give
+\[
+(x,y,z;k)\in
+\{(0,0,0;0),\ \pm(C,d,-1;0),
+\ \pm(-b,C,d;1),\ \pm(C,C-1,d;1)\}.
+\]
+Indeed, for $k=0$ one has $|z|\le1$, and $z=1$ forces
+$(x,y)=(-C,-d)$.  For $k=1$, the inequality at $z\le a-2$ forces $z=d$;
+reducing $x+ay=aC-b$ modulo $a$ leaves precisely
+$(x,y)=(-b,C)$ and $(C,C-1)$.  The terminal pairs are
+$(0,0)$, $\pm(d,-1)$, $\pm(C,d)$, and $\pm(C-1,d)$.  Neither
+$\pm(-b,C)$ nor $\pm(C,C-1)$ is terminal.  The remaining type
+$\pm(C,d,-1)$ forces a preceding $\pm(-b,C,d)$, whose initial pair is not
+terminal.
+
+Thus, in either chamber, a nonzero triple cannot persist through all three
+overlaps.  Reading the three equations backwards forces
+$e_2=e_3=e_4=0$, then $e_1=0$, and finally $e_0=0$.

 \begin{abstract}
-We determine exact overlap thresholds and local inverse structure for cyclic
-language-rank recodings of quadratic and simple-Parry beta-languages.  A
-legal length-$m$ word is identified with its colexicographic positional rank;
-the same rank is evaluated on the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number
-of legal words, returned to the legal language, and overlapped along the
-shift.  This is cyclic reduction of integer language ranks, not numerical
-$\beta$-normalization.
-
-The Fibonacci model has sharp nontrivial threshold three.  We give its
-explicit three-window decoder, low-window counterexamples, and complete
-two-window branch locus.  For every quadratic Pisot base, the least
-nontrivial aperture is three exactly for the roots of
-$x^2-ax-a$ and $x^2-ax+1$, and is two otherwise.  We also determine chamber
-duality, future-only inverse bounds, the critical two-fixed-point normal
-form, exact finite-block onset, the canonical right Fischer cover, and exact
-Markov order in the stabilized alphabet.  The metallic family becomes a
-transparent specialization of this classification.
+We study sliding recodings obtained by reducing colexicographic language
+ranks modulo the number of legal words and overlapping the resulting finite
+windows.  For every quadratic Pisot $\beta$-language, the least nontrivial
+injective aperture is three precisely for the roots of $x^2-ax-a$ and
+$x^2-ax+1$, and is two otherwise.  The future-only inverse length is three in
+the positive-conjugate chamber and two in the negative chamber at aperture
+three; for negative conjugate and aperture $m\ge4$ we prove the bounds
+$2\le\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)\le m$.
 
 For every nonintegral simple-Parry base, a coordinatewise-difference quotient
-of the classical pair graph preserves every collision and gives an exact
-longest-path formula for future-only inverse depth.  We derive the complete
-aperture-two trichotomy without a Pisot hypothesis.  Applied to Bassino's
-cubic simple-Parry Pisot family, the quotient gives injective apertures
-$m_n=n-1$ with exact future-only inverse length $n-1$, hence unbounded depth
-across the family.
+of the classical pair graph preserves all collisions.  Its longest directed
+paths give the future-only inverse length, while reachable cycles decide
+noninjectivity; the resulting aperture-two trichotomy needs no Pisot
+hypothesis.  In Bassino's cubic simple-Parry Pisot family, the quotient gives
+injective apertures $m_n=n-1$ with
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta_n,m_n)=n-1$, so future-only inverse depth is unbounded
+across cubic systems.  The Fibonacci decoder, chamber duality, critical
+Fischer covers, and Markov orders follow as concrete consequences of these
+two collision mechanisms.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}
 \label{sec:intro}
 
-Finite-window recodings can collapse individual input words and still become
-invertible when their outputs are overlapped.  This paper determines where
-that transition occurs, how much future output a memory-zero inverse needs,
-and what local shift structure remains at and below threshold for quadratic
-and simple-Parry beta-languages.
+Finite-window recodings may collapse isolated input words and nevertheless
+become invertible after their outputs are overlapped.  We determine this
+transition for cyclic rank recodings of quadratic and simple-Parry
+$\beta$-languages, together with the amount of future output needed by a
+memory-zero inverse.
 
-Let $X_m$ be the legal words of length $m$ in a greedy numeration language,
-ordered colexicographically.  Positional rank identifies $X_m$ with
-$\{0,\ldots,Q_m-1\}$, where $Q_m=|X_m|$.  We evaluate the same weighted rank
-on the full digit cube, reduce it modulo $Q_m$, and return the legal word with
-that residue.  Overlapping these cyclically recoded windows defines a sliding
-factor $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ and its image $Y_{\beta,m}$.  Positional rank belongs
-to Parry--Bertrand numeration theory
+Let $X_m$ be the legal length-$m$ words in a greedy numeration language,
+ordered colexicographically, and put $Q_m=|X_m|$.  Positional rank identifies
+$X_m$ with $\{0,\ldots,Q_m-1\}$.  We evaluate the same weighted rank on the
+full digit cube, reduce it modulo $Q_m$, and return the legal word carrying
+that residue.  Overlapping these recoded windows defines a sliding factor
+$\Phi_{\beta,m}$ with image $Y_{\beta,m}$.  Positional ranks come from
+Parry--Bertrand numeration
 \cite{BertrandMathis1989,BruyereHansel1997,LecomteRigo2001,
-CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}; reduction modulo the finite-language count
-is the operation classified here.
+CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}; the cyclic reduction and its overlap
+structure are the objects studied here.  These are congruences of integer
+language ranks, not equalities of numerical $\beta$-values.
 
-The construction must not be confused with numerical
-$\beta$-normalization.  The congruences compare integer language ranks, not
-values in $\mathbb Z[\beta]$.  Nor is the rank-relabelled local rule a linear
-cellular automaton: the input alphabet is a proper digit subset of
-$\mathbb Z/Q_m\mathbb Z$, not a module on which the rule is a group
-endomorphism.
+The local rule is arithmetic, but injectivity is a collision problem.  In
+the quadratic case the language-count recurrence separates bounded sliding
+congruences directly.  In the simple-Parry case the same collision problem
+closes on a finite quotient of the classical pair graph.  The two parts of
+the paper are therefore different arithmetic realizations of one symbolic
+mechanism: a nonzero difference path records two raw inputs with the same
+overlapped output, and finite extinction of every such path gives a
+future-only decoder.
 
-\medskip
-\noindent\textbf{The Fibonacci model.}
-The first part develops the binary prototype completely.  The finite-window
-rank is the Fibonacci value
-\[
-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}F_{j+2}x_j\pmod {F_{m+2}},
-\]
-and legal words contain no adjacent ones.  Lemma~\ref{lem:m3-decoder} gives
-an explicit decoder from three consecutive recoded windows.
-Theorem~\ref{thm:block-invertibility} proves that aperture three is the exact
-nontrivial threshold, while Proposition~\ref{prop:low-window-counterexamples}
-gives the sharp finite-block failures below onset.  At aperture two,
-Theorem~\ref{thm:m2-branch-locus} shows that the only nonsingleton fiber
-identifies the two constant binary points.  This model isolates the mechanism
-later seen at every extremal quadratic parameter.
-
-\medskip
-\noindent\textbf{The quadratic classification.}
-Every quadratic Pisot number lies in one of the chambers
+\begin{introtheorem}[Quadratic threshold classification]
+Let $\beta$ be a quadratic Pisot number, and use the greedy language and
+cyclic Parry rank of Definition~\ref{def:quadratic-parry-fold}.  Then
 \[
-x^2-ax-b,\quad a\ge b\ge1,
-\qquad\text{or}\qquad
-x^2-ax+b,\quad a\ge3,\ 1\le b\le a-2.
-\]
-After deriving the exact Parry words and rank recurrences, we prove a
-nearest-multiple separation and a bounded sliding-congruence lemma.  They
-lead to Theorem~\ref{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}:
-\[
 m_*(\beta)=3
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{minpoly}(\beta)\in
 \{x^2-ax-a:a\ge1\}\cup\{x^2-ax+1:a\ge3\},
 \]
-and $m_*(\beta)=2$ otherwise.  Thus the exceptional negative chamber is the
-metallic family, with its golden boundary member, and the exceptional
-positive chamber is its critical dual.
+and $m_*(\beta)=2$ otherwise.  For every $m\ge m_*(\beta)$ and $n\ge m$,
+the length-$n$ block map is injective, $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is a conjugacy onto
+its SFT image, and its inverse has memory zero and anticipation at most
+$m-1$.
+\end{introtheorem}
+
+This is Theorem~\ref{thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold}.  The exceptional
+families are exactly the two loci where the aperture-two map identifies the
+constant zero and maximal-digit points.  Away from them, two consecutive
+outputs admit an explicit decoder.  At and above threshold, the same
+arithmetic gives finite-block onset, the right Fischer cover, and the Markov
+order of the image.  Future-only depth is more delicate: Theorem
+\ref{thm:quadratic-optimal-causal-inverse} gives the value three throughout
+the positive-conjugate chamber, the value two in the negative chamber at
+aperture three, and only
+$2\le\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)\le m$ in the negative chamber for $m\ge4$.
+
+The Fibonacci system is the smallest exceptional parameter.  Its explicit
+three-window decoder supplies a readable prototype for the general
+recurrence argument, while its aperture-two branch consists only of the two
+constant binary points.  The metallic family is recorded later as a direct
+quadratic specialization rather than as an independent classification.
